title: Latency decomposition and quantile-guided scheduler notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an exploratory run where we (a) break down end-to-end latency into queueing / service / preemption components, (b) sweep scheduler knobs using a quantile-oriented objective function, and (c) validate results against real traffic replays. The goal is pragmatic: find a set of continuous-batching scheduler heuristics that improve p95 and p99 for conversational tail-heavy workloads without regressing p50 more than 5%.

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Static timeouts tuned to average arrival rates harm tails under bursty traffic; adaptive timeout that factors recent inter-arrival quantiles will reduce p99.
2) Including an age-penalty in the batch formation objective (soft fairness) reduces long-tail queueing at the cost of slightly lower batch utilization.
3) Preemption thresholding interacts with small-batch path overheads; lowering preemption aggressiveness for short sequences reduces p95 for short-request traffic.

Experiment harness and measurement approach:
- Harness: replay tool that consumes request traces and emits into local scheduler harness; identical runtime image to production (serving-runtime:v2026-02-16-experiments).
- Hardware: 4x A100-40GB nodes (dev pool), identical kernel and CUDA stack.
- Workloads: three profiles:
  * convo-burst: conversational mixed-length, heavy short-turns, synthetic bursts from production traces (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-24).
  * low-qps-steady: 10 RPS steady, long sequences (512 tokens).
  * mixed-latency: mixture 70% short/30% long with Poisson jitter.
- Traffic shaping: Poisson arrival baseline; additional experiments with Pareto bursts (alpha=1.5) and scheduled microbursts (20x baseline for 5s).
- Metrics collected (per run): p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, queueing time distribution, service time distribution, batch size distribution, batch utilization, GPU occupancy, preemption rate, throughput (tokens/sec). Tracing captured queue_start, batch_form, kernel_start, token_emit spans.
- Objective function: quantile-weighted score = 0.6*p95 + 0.4*p99 (lower is better). Secondary objective: keep p50 change >= -5% (i.e., not worse than 5% regression).

Knobs swept (discrete + continuous):
- timeout_ms: [4, 8, 12, 20, 40]
- soft_age_penalty: [0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5] (higher favors older items)
- max_batch_size: [16, 32, 64, 128]
- preemption_threshold_ms: [0, 5, 10, 20] (0 = immediate preempt)
- quantile-window-seconds (for adaptive timeout): [5, 15, 60]
- adaptive-timeout-factor: [0.5, 1.0, 1.5] (multiplier on observed inter-arrival q90)

Key procedural notes:
- Each configuration ran for 30 minutes with warmup 5 minutes, repeated 3x for variance estimates.
- We seed RNG for synthetic mixes and store trace ids in gs://redwood-experiments/serving/quantile-harness/2026-02-28.tar.gz.
- All runs logged to Prometheus + local JSON dump. Analysis scripts: git pr 5123.

Important observations and measured decompositions:
1) Queueing vs service time decomposition: for convo-burst profile, p99 end-to-end was dominated by queueing (median queueing share at p99 ~72%). Service time variance contributed ~20% to tail. This confirms queue-centric tuning is high leverage.
2) Adaptive timeout using q90 inter-arrival produced a ~22% reduction in p99 vs best static timeout (20ms), while increasing p50 by ~2.8% (within target). The best config: adaptive-timeout-factor=1.0 with quantile-window-seconds=15.
3) Soft age penalty (0.25) reduced the number of requests with queueing >50ms by 40% in burst windows, but batch utilization dropped ~6%. Net quantile score improved for convo-burst but regressed slightly for low-qps-steady.
4) Preemption_threshold_ms=0 (immediate preempt) had a measurable negative effect on p95 for short-sequence heavy loads: preemption caused head-of-line reorders and extra kernel setup; raising threshold to 10ms removed that regression.
5) Max_batch_size had diminishing returns above 64 for our workload mix; 64 hit the sweet spot for throughput vs latency in steady long-sequence tests.

Representative run (convo-burst) summary: best quantile-weighted score config -> timeout adaptive (q90, window 15s, factor 1.0), soft_age_penalty=0.25, max_batch_size=64, preemption_threshold_ms=10. Results vs baseline (prod-default):
- p50: +2.8%
- p95: -18.4%
- p99: -21.9%
- batch utilization: -5.9%
- throughput (tokens/sec): -3.2%
This meets constraints and gives strong tail improvements.

Surprises / gotchas:
- Tracing artifacts: some queue_start spans were missing for short-lived requests when a local client-side retry happened; we added a guard in the harness to suppress duplicate trace ids. This impacted one early run (run id: 2026-02-28-07).
- Preemption interactions with quantization path: when batches included mixed-quantized and fp16 requests, preemption created kernel reinitializations that magnified tail latency. Workaround: prefer batch homogenization before preempting.
- Under very low steady QPS, soft_age_penalty induced unnecessary reorders reducing throughput; need conditional logic to disable age-penalty when measured arrival variance < threshold.

Recommendations (short term):
1) Prototype adaptive-timeout using q90(window=15s) factor=1.0 in a canary fleet for convo-heavy routes. Enable a circuit that falls back to static timeout if observed inter-arrival variance drops below X.
2) Default soft_age_penalty to 0.0, but enable per-route override and a dynamic trigger (burst detector) to flip it to 0.25 during bursts.
3) Increase preemption_threshold_ms to 10ms for short-sequence-optimized runtimes; add route-level knob for long-sequence routes to keep lower threshold.
4) Cap max_batch_size to 64 for general-purpose pools; allow dedicated pools for throughput-heavy customers to raise this.

Follow-ups and next experiments:
- Run longer multi-day replay against real production traces (one-week windows) to measure burst recurrence effects and stability of adaptive timeout. (Ticket INF-2438).
- Experiment with hybrid objective that includes cost: include tokens/sec and GPU occupancy penalty to avoid hidden throughput regressions.
- Implement batch-homogenization heuristic (group by quantization path) and re-run top configs; hypothesize it reduces p99 further by avoiding kernel churn.
- Add small probe traffic (micro-probes) to maintain timestamp freshness for quantile estimation during very quiet periods.

Action items / TODOs:
- Diego: add guard to trace collector and re-run the three failed seeds (blocker: missing spans) by 2026-03-12.
- Priya: wire canary rollout plan and add route-level dynamic age-penalty toggle to console by 2026-03-20.
- Evan: prototype batch-homogenization patch and measure kernel_restart_count.
- Ava: prepare an experiment brief for infra and SRE with suggested rollout window and rollback criteria.

Notes to self (informal):
- Save raw json dumps under gs://redwood-experiments/serving/runs/quantile-sweep/2026-02-28/ and keep one snapshot in the repo artifacts folder.
- Visuals we need: CDF breakdown of queueing/service by quantile (p50/p90/p95/p99), waterfall trace for three p99 examples pre/post.
- Keep the quantile window conservative; too-short windows chase noise in microbursty traffic.

Unresolved questions:
- Optimal mechanism to detect burst onset robustly without too many false positives.
- Interplay between adaptive timeout and cross-route routing (when we reroute to cheaper model variants): will adaptive timeouts cause more fallbacks? Need separate experiment.
- How batch-homogenization affects fairness for multi-tenant pools.

Appendix (quick commands and links):
- Replay command: ./harness/replay.sh --trace gs://redwood-experiments/serving/traces/convo-burst-2026-02-20.json --config configs/quantile-sweep.yaml --out runs/2026-02-28
- Analysis notebook: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/notebooks/quantile-sweep-analysis.ipynb (PR 5123)
